Pembina County sits in northeast North Dakota, along the Canadian border. Its county seat is Cavalier. For tax sale buyers, this county is worth study because sales can include small town lots, rural land, and county held property. This guide explains how Pembina County tax deed sales work. It uses county records, state law, and official public sources only.

What Is Pembina County Tax Deed Investing?

Pembina County does not sell normal tax lien certificates to private buyers. North Dakota law now uses a county tax deed process for real property. The county first takes tax title after the legal notice process. Then it sells county held property at public auction. NDACo states that North Dakota has not allowed private lien holder interest in delinquent taxes since 1999.

Important Details and Links

Key Takeaways

  • Pembina County, located in northeast North Dakota, follows a tax deed sales process rather than selling tax lien certificates.
  • The annual tax deed auction typically occurs on the third Tuesday in November at 11:00 a.m. in the county courthouse in Cavalier.
  • Investors should conduct thorough due diligence before bidding to avoid issues with title, access, and repairs.
  • Buyers can purchase over-the-counter tax deeds after the auction if properties remain unsold.
  • This market may appeal to careful buyers looking for low-entry price properties and potential high returns.

The annual sale is set by state law for the third Tuesday in November. Pembina County agendas and minutes show the sale set at 11:00 a.m. in the courthouse. County contacts list Auditor Treasurer Melissa Gapp at 701 265 4231 and gappmelissa@nd.gov.

Fun Facts About Pembina County

• Pembina County has about 6,600 residents.
• Cavalier is the county seat.
• The county says agriculture is the backbone of its economy.
• The county also has manufacturing plants and three ports of entry into Canada.
• Census data shows a median owner occupied home value near $119,000.

Attractions and Economic Highlights

• Attractions: Icelandic State Park, Lake Renwick, Gunlogson Arboretum, and the Pembina County Historical Society Museum.
• Transportation: Interstate 29, North Dakota Highways 5, 18, and 32, plus Canadian border ports.
• Economy: Farming, crop handling, manufacturing, retail, and border trade.
• Community: Fishing, boating, skiing, snowmobiling, and small town events.

Why Is Pembina County Good for Tax Deed Investors?

• Small county sales may have less bidder attention.
• Some parcels have low minimum bids.
• Tax deed buyers may find high returns through resale or rental use.
• This can be a low risk investment only when research is strong.
• North Dakota state tax lien opportunities are really tax deed sales now.
• Low price does not mean low risk. Title, access, use, and cleanup still matter.

Auction Process for Pembina County Tax Deed Sales

Pembina County tax deed sales follow North Dakota Chapter 57 28. Before sale, the county appraises property and sets a minimum sale price. Notice must include the legal description, street address if any, and minimum price. The county posts notice at the auditor’s office at least fifteen days before sale. It also publishes notice in the official county newspaper.

How the Auction Works

  1. Step 1: Check the sale notice

    Read every parcel description. Confirm the minimum bid. Check taxes, specials, access, and use.

  2. Step 2: Confirm you can bid

    State law says a person cannot be the highest bidder if that person owes delinquent taxes to any county. Pembina County also read a sale rule that bidders must be current on property taxes.

  3. Step 3: Attend the sale

    The sale is usually in the Farmer’s Room at the courthouse. Plan to arrive early. No official advance registration window was found.

  4. Step 4: Bid the parcel

    This is not a bid down interest sale. There is no starting interest rate. Each parcel is sold to the highest qualified bidder at or above the minimum price.

  5. Step 5: Pay on time

    Pembina County’s recent sale rule said all payments were due by close of business by cash or cashier’s check.

Maximum Potential Returns and Expected Returns

Pembina County tax deed returns come from buying below market value. They do not come from lien interest. In one recent sale record, many bids were small. Some lots received bids from $50 to $1,000. One Mountain City lot received a $4,000 bid. That shows why this market can interest patient buyers. It also shows why each parcel needs careful study.

The maximum return is not capped by a certificate rate. It depends on purchase price, title work, repairs, resale value, and holding time. If the county uses a contract for deed, state law caps that contract interest at 12%. Recent Pembina terms asked for same day cash or cashier’s check.

Open to All Investors and Foreign Investor Participation

The official rules found do not show a local residency rule. The main bidder limit is tax status. A bidder cannot owe delinquent taxes to any county. This means local buyers, out of state buyers, and international investors may be able to take part. Still, foreign investor participation needs planning. You may need a U.S. mailing address, funds ready in the right form, and help with recording, insurance, and resale. Always confirm with the Auditor Treasurer before the sale.

Importance of Due Diligence in Pembina County Tax Deed Investing

What Due Diligence Entails

• Read the county notice and legal description.
• Check the GIS parcel map.
• Drive by the property when allowed.
• Confirm road access.
• Review taxes, specials, and utilities.
• Order a title search.
• Ask about city code issues.
• Check floodplain and drainage concerns.

Risks of Skipping Due Diligence

• You may buy land with no useful access.
• Cleanup may cost more than the land.
• Old structures may be unsafe.
• A quiet title case may be needed.
• Special assessments may still matter.
• Resale may take longer than expected.

Buying Over the Counter Tax Deeds in Pembina County

How to Purchase OTC Tax Deeds

North Dakota law allows property not sold at the annual November sale to be sold by private sale before the next annual sale. The county auditor may sell it for at least the minimum sale price. Pembina County records show that some parcels can receive no bid. Call the Auditor Treasurer after the sale and ask if any county held parcels remain available.

Benefits of OTC Purchases

Over the counter buys can reduce bidding pressure. You may have more time to study the parcel. You still need title work, access checks, and a written answer from the county on price and payment.

Why Pembina County Is a Top Choice for Tax Deed Investors

Economic and Tax Advantages

• The county has strong farm roots.
• Crop production supports local land demand.
• Border access helps trade and services.
• Lower home values may help entry level buyers.
• Small town parcels can fit cash buyers.

Real Estate Market Overview

Pembina County is not a fast flip market. It is better for careful buyers who like low entry prices and rural or small city parcels. Census data shows lower median home values than many U.S. markets. That can help investors with smaller budgets. It can also mean slower resale. Plan for holding time.

Conclusion

Pembina County, North Dakota tax deed sales are best for careful buyers. The county uses a tax deed process, not a normal tax lien certificate sale. The auction is usually held on the third Tuesday in November at 11:00 a.m. Central Time. The common site is the courthouse in Cavalier.

The main benefit is simple. You may be able to buy property at a low price. The main risk is also simple. Cheap property can have title, access, repair, or resale issues. Smart investing starts with thorough research. Call the Auditor Treasurer. Read the notice. Study each parcel before bidding.

Pro Tips for Pembina County Tax Deed Buyers

• Watch the commission agendas in early November. Sale items often appear there.
• Study small city lots in Bathgate, Mountain, Neche, St. Thomas, and Walhalla.
• Check farm access roads before bidding on rural land.
• Ask if any parcel has unpaid special assessments.
• Bring cashier’s check options if the county requires same day payment.

FAQs About Pembina County Tax Deeds

• Do I need quiet title after buying?

Many buyers do. Ask a North Dakota real estate attorney.

• Can I get title insurance right away?

Maybe not. Tax deed property may need extra title work.

• Can I enter the property after purchase?

Confirm deed status first. Handle occupied property through legal steps.

• Can I finance a tax deed purchase?

Do not count on it. Same day payment may be required.

• Can I resell right away?

You can try. Title issues may slow the sale.
